_readme: Registry of scheduled NetSuite reports ingested into persistent report memory. source=email: fetched from rpa@wego.com Gmail (sender system@sent-via.netsuite.com) by subject substring. source=cabinet: pulled from the File Cabinet via get_cabinet_file. period_format tells the agent how to normalise the period a user asks for. Add entries as Nikhil supplies each report's subject/folder; keep report_key stable — it is the storage path.
subsidiaries: WeGo Saudi for Travel and Tourism
_subsidiaries_note: Official NetSuite subsidiary names (Nikhil 2026-07-28). Used by get_stored_report(subsidiary=...) to resolve what the user typed to the exact 'Subsidiary: Name' value before filtering. 'consolidated'/'consolidate'/no subsidiary mentioned = serve the stored consolidated file unfiltered.

reports.title: A/P Aging Detail BK Wego (Consolidated)
reports.subject_contains: AP: A/P Aging Detail BK Wego (Consolidated)
reports.period_notes: Subject carries 'as of DD/MM/YYYY' (e.g. 'as of 30/06/2026'); the fetcher normalises it to 2026-06-30. When a user asks 'as of 30/06/2026' or 'for June end', resolve to the ISO date before calling get_stored_report.
reports.notes: Subject prefix 'AP:' is the DOMAIN tag — identifies which channel/team the report belongs to. Report name is 'A/P Aging Detail BK Wego'. Default variant is (Consolidated); if the user names NO subsidiary, serve this one. Per-subsidiary variants will be registered later — if a user asks for a specific subsidiary before those exist, say that variant isn't ingested yet (do NOT serve Consolidated as a substitute without saying so). Attachment arrives as generic 'report.xls' — the period path keeps versions apart; meta.subject holds provenance. This is the report that CANNOT be rebuilt via SuiteQL (report-engine only) — serving this NetSuite-generated file is the only correct source.
example_questions: AP aging detail BK consolidated as of 30/06/2026
A/P aging report for June end
reports.subject_note: Matched with whitespace collapsed + case-insensitive, so the real subject's DOUBLE space between 'BK' and 'Wego' is handled. Keep the FULL subject including '(Consolidated)': a truncated 'AP: A/P Aging Detail BK' would also match per-subsidiary variants and file them under this consolidated key.
reports.attachment_format_note: NetSuite's scheduled export is now report.CSV (was report.xls). Any format is ingested; delivery always converts to .xlsx (rows verbatim, only cell types/formats change) so finance gets Excel.
reports.refresh_note: refresh=always: re-check the inbox on EVERY request even if the period is already stored — Akansha re-sends/reschedules, so the newest email for a period supersedes what we hold. Newest wins (same key/period/filename is overwritten).
reports.subsidiary_subject_template: AP: A/P Aging Detail BK {subsidiary} as of
reports.subsidiary_note: Since 2026-07-30 Akansha schedules a SEPARATE email per subsidiary: 'AP: A/P Aging Detail BK <Subsidiary> as of DD/MM/YYYY' with report.csv attached. These are PREFERRED over filtering the consolidated file: NetSuite segregates the rows itself, so the '- No Vendor -' / '- No Subsidiary -' block is attributed correctly and nothing has to be inferred. Matching is anchored on 'BK <subsidiary> as of' (normalised whitespace, case-insensitive) so 'Wego' cannot swallow 'Wego Middle East'. Filtering the consolidated export remains only as a FALLBACK when a subsidiary's email is absent, and is flagged as derived. Extraction is pure Python stdlib + openpyxl — NO AI tokens.
subsidiary_variants: WeGo Saudi for Travel and Tourism
reports.subsidiary_variants_note: EXACT scope names as they appear in the subject between 'BK ' and ' as of' (Nikhil 2026-07-30, from the inbox screenshots). The subject IS the mapping: 'AP: A/P Aging Detail BK PT Wego Travel Indonesia as of 30/07/2026' -> scope 'PT Wego Travel Indonesia'. THREE Singapore variants are DISTINCT reports — 'Wego Pte Ltd (Singapore)', '... (Singapore) (Consolidated)' and '... (SG Group) (Consolidated)' — never collapse them. Resolve the user's words against THIS list only: exact match first, else a UNIQUE substring; anything ambiguous or unknown -> ask, listing the candidates. Never guess a scope for finance data.
